papers.titleEn: Vesicle-Surface Recognition Coupled with Graphdiyne-zyme Arrays for Marker-Independent Colorimetric Fingerprinting of Bacterial Extracellular Vesicles
papers.abstract: Abstract Bacterial extracellular vesicles (bEVs) that encode disease-relevant molecular information are released into body fluids at early stages of infection, rendering them promising biomarkers for early diagnosis. However, the lack of universal surface markers causes limitation of conventional antibody-based strategies, severely restricting the use of bEVs for early diagnosis. Here, we report a marker-independent recognition strategy that translates the interfacial heterogeneity of bEV membranes into amplified catalytic signatures. Graphdiyne-zyme sensor arrays are designed and constructed, in which the graphdiyne spatially fixes and organizes three kinds of metal oxides to form multiple nanozymes with confined, multivalent catalytic interfaces. By coupling vesicle-surface recognition with graphdiyne-zyme arrays, the interfaces efficiently transform subtle membrane variations into distinct colorimetric fingerprints. The graphdiyne-zyme array generated distinguishable colorimetric fingerprints for bEVs from six UTI-associated bacterial species and, when integrated with an XGBoost classifier, achieved an accuracy of 96.9% in a clinical test set comprising 32 samples. This study establishes an analytical framework for the marker-independent recognition of bEVs, delivering an alternative approach to replace conventional affinity-based biosensing strategies.
papers.filename: Chunxian Guo, Anal. Chem., 2026, Vesicle-Surface Recognition Coupled with Graphdiyne-zyme Arrays for Marker-Independent Colorimetric Fingerprinting of Bacterial Extracellular Vesic

papers.titleEn: Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
papers.abstract: Abstract Solution-processed thin films of colloidal lead halide perovskite (LHP) nanocrystals (NCs) show great potential for next-generation optoelectronic devices. However, these NC solids exhibit non-negligible size and shape polydispersity, which introduces both structural and energetic disorder. Here we resolve the exciton dynamics in space, time, and energy to elucidate the impact of disorder on exciton transport. We show that the disorder depends sensitively on the alkylamine ligand used in the synthesis. While shorter alkyl chain lengths lead to high polydispersity, longer alkyl chains lead to a narrower size distribution and smaller particles where quantum confinement becomes more pronounced, consequently leading to increased energetic disorder. Strikingly, we find that exciton transport is less efficient in NC solids with long alkyl chains, despite the fact that they have significantly more narrowly size-distributed ensembles. This demonstrates that energetic disorder rather than structural disorder is the dominant factor for predicting exciton transport within these disordered systems.
papers.filename: Ferry Prins, Nano Lett., 2026, Exciton Transport in Disordered Perovskite Nanocrystal Solids
